MCD.rationale: MCD is a high-quality, asset-light franchise with industry-leading operating margins (~47%), robust and accelerating cash generation (OCF +25.3% YoY), and a structurally recovering equity base. The business fundamentals are solid: ~3% revenue growth, margin expansion, and a massive digital loyalty ecosystem (~210M active users driving 2.5x visit frequency). However, the thesis is qualified by two material headwinds: (1) the oil price shock (+76% in 90 days to $108.64/bbl) represents an unquantified but potentially significant input-cost risk to franchisee economics that has not yet appeared in reported financials, and (2) valuation cannot be rigorously assessed due to broken PE data in the raw pack, though third-party estimates suggest ~22.7x forward earnings — reasonable for a quality compounder but not clearly cheap. The stock sits in the lower quartile of its 251-bar range ($293.59 vs. $341.75 high), and Q1 2026 earnings on May 7 with consensus EPS of $2.75 and revenue of $6.48B could serve as a near-term catalyst if results confirm continued momentum. The score reflects strong fundamental health and trajectory (pillar 1) tempered by a fair-to-slightly-cheap but unverifiable valuation (pillar 2) and a modest near-term catalyst from the upcoming earnings report (pillar 3).
